explanation: The 6th Knesset was elected in November 1965 (government formed January 1966). 1969 is the 7th Knesset's year, so it appears twice.

explanation: Golda Meir's term as Foreign Minister ended on 12 January 1966, the day Eshkol's 13th government was formed. No woman sat in that government at its start.

Inconsistent with the other rows: the 8th Knesset was elected on 31 December 1973. 1974 is the year Golda Meir's government was formed (10 March 1974). Keep 1974 only if the column is meant to show the government's formation year.

explanation: Golda Meir's 16th government (March 1974) had one woman, Meir herself. Shulamit Aloni joined only in Rabin's next government (3 June 1974), when Meir was no longer in it.

explanation: Begin's 2nd government (August 1981) had no women. Sarah Doron became Minister without Portfolio in July 1983 and was described as the first woman in the cabinet since Aloni resigned in 1974. (One biography gives 1981, but most sources give 1983.)

explanation: Sarah Doron's term ended in September 1984, when Peres's unity government was formed (13 September 1984). Shoshana Arbeli-Almozlino became Health Minister only on 20 October 1986.

explanation: Barak's government (6 July 1999) started with one woman, Dalia Itzik (Environment). Yuli Tamir joined on 5 August 1999, so even counting her the total is 2, not 5.

explanation: Sharon's 2nd government (28 February 2003) had three women: Limor Livnat (Education), Tzipi Livni (Immigrant Absorption) and Yehudit Naot (Environment).
